correctness.rationale: Independently replayed RESULT.md §§1–4, including the nonstandard local-tail step, without assuming a rate density or relying on a cosine Tauberian converse. For a finite sum of J independent integrated-rate contributions, an exceedance of z with no term above (1−ε)z requires one term above z/J and another above εz/(J−1), giving O(z^{-2α}); union bounds and ε↓0 give the exact C_t. For the free unit-intensity lattice kernel p_a(n), exponential tilting of Fourier inversion bounds it by C e^{-n/4} for a<n and C a^{-1/2}e^{-n²/(4a)} for a≥n. Untilted inversion gives n p_{n²u}(n)→(2πu)^{-1/2}exp(−1/(2u)) uniformly on compact positive u-intervals. The measures n^{2α}Law(A_t/n²) converge vaguely to αC_t u^{-1−α}du. For small u the exponential kernel bound summed on dyadic intervals is negligible, and for u≥M the rescaled bound is O(M^{-α−1/2}). Integrating the limiting kernel gives exactly K_t=α2^α C_t Γ(α+1/2)/√π. Reflection conditioned on the independent unrestricted clock gives the exact 2m-site telescoped window, not a subtraction of asymptotic equivalents. Survival is positive; dividing by it gives the conditional coefficient and tail integration gives the strict q cutoff, including logarithmic divergence at equality. Each absorbed bounded-step martingale has mean m, so averaging over the clock preserves the first moment even for infinite mean count. Independently, Mittag–Leffler operational survival is comparable to (1+a)^{-1/2}, by its reflected sum over the fixed sites 1−m through m and the local central limit. At n refresh periods its mixture is comparable to ∫ s^{-1/2}e^{-s}(1+(τs)^α)^{-n}ds, hence to n^{-1/(2α)} by small-s scaling. Summing the monotone survival curve proves the mean-lifetime cutoff including α=1/2. Its rate tail has C=1/Γ(1−α) by the monotone Laplace tail theorem. The two integrability thresholds are therefore complementary exactly as stated. Detailed replay is in /workspace/branches/survivor-tail-proof.md. The supplied Pareto/Bessel diagnostic was inspected, not executed; no finite check is used for the equivalent.
